Get help with using Qalqon, protection, children, time limits and settings.

Qalqon is an offline-first, privacy-first parental control app. A parent creates a local account, enrolls their own face and their children\'s faces, and picks protected apps. The device recognises who is holding it: a parent sees no restrictions, a child gets blocked, and an unknown user follows the chosen fallback policy. All face processing happens on-device and no internet connection is required.

1. Choose your language. 2. Create an account with your name, phone number and a PIN. 3. Set up the parent profile. 4. Add a child. 5. Choose the protected apps. 6. Turn protection on in Settings > Protection.
Open Settings > Appearance and choose Uzbek, English or Russian. The app changes immediately and remembers your choice.

Open Settings > Protection and turn on Protection enabled. Protection needs a signed-in account, the draw-over-other-apps permission, Usage Access and the background monitoring service; the Protection screen lists whichever of these is still missing.
Open Settings > Protection and turn off Protection enabled. Protection stops and the ongoing notification disappears. You can turn it back on at any time.
Open the Children tab and press Add (＋). Enter the child name, choose a restriction level and save. Open the child card to see all of that child’s settings.
Open the Children tab, press the menu (⋮) on the child card and choose Enroll face — or open the child and use the Face row. Hold the face in the frame in good light until the capture completes.
Open Settings > Protection > Protected apps, find the app and tick it. Protected apps stay locked for the child while protection is running.
Open Settings > Protection > Protected apps and press Refresh apps. The list is read from the apps installed on this device; apps installed later appear after a refresh.
Open a child’s detail screen and choose Screen time. You can set a total daily limit and per-category limits. Usage is shown for the child selected as the screen-time target.
Open a child’s detail screen and choose Schedule. Add a schedule with a name, days, a start and end time and the apps it affects. The active schedule is shown on the Home dashboard.
Open a child’s detail screen and choose Eye safety. Enable it and set the warning and danger actions to limit long, close-up screen use.

The parent area is protected by your QALQON PIN. On a device with an enrolled fingerprint or face, the unlock screen asks for biometrics first; the PIN is always available as the fallback using the Use PIN button.
When a child asks for extra time from the protection screen, the request appears in the Activity tab and in a notification. Open the Requests screen to approve or reject it.

Qalqon works fully offline: nothing is sent to a server. Face recognition runs on the device and only a mathematical template is kept, never the image. You can delete face data and all local data in Settings > Privacy.
Yes. Qalqon is offline-first: it has no internet permission and never sends data to a server. Face recognition and all settings work fully on the device.
Why does biometric access appear first?
The unlock screen offers the Android biometric prompt first on devices that have an enrolled fingerprint or face, because it is faster. The PIN is always available with the Use PIN button.
How do I sign in with the PIN?
On the unlock screen press Use PIN, type your QALQON PIN and press Unlock. The PIN is the 4 or 6 digit code you chose when creating the account.
How do I enroll a face?
Open a child from the Children tab (or the parent profile from Settings > Family) and use the Face row or Enroll face action, then follow the on-screen guidance.
How do I add a child?
Open the Children tab, press Add (＋), enter the name, choose the restriction level and save.
How do I protect an app?
Open Settings > Protection > Protected apps, find the app and tick it.
How do I turn protection on?
Open Settings > Protection and turn on Protection enabled. The screen shows any permission that still needs to be granted.
How do I turn protection off?
Open Settings > Protection and turn off Protection enabled.
Entirely on this device, in Qalqon’s private storage. Nothing is uploaded, and there is no cloud account.
How do I refresh the app list?
Open Settings > Protection > Protected apps and press Refresh apps.
An app is missing from the list
The list shows apps installed for this device that can be launched. Press Refresh apps. If it still does not appear, it may be a system or hidden app that Qalqon filters out.
I cannot enroll a child’s face
Check that the camera permission is allowed, use good, even light and hold the face inside the frame, then try again. A child without an enrolled face cannot be recognised for protection.
The camera must see a face. Check the lens is clean, the room is not too dark and the face is not too close or too far. Recognition runs only while protection is active.
Open Settings > Protection and check that Protection enabled is on and that every required permission shows as granted. Qalqon protection is listed as active on the Home dashboard when it is running.
A protected app is not blocked
Check that protection is on, the app is ticked in Protected apps, and the child’s face is enrolled. A child-specific policy on the child’s Apps screen overrides the global list.
Open Settings > Notifications and check that they are enabled. On Android 13 and newer the notification permission must be allowed for Qalqon.
Biometrics need an enrolled fingerprint or face in the device settings. When biometrics are unavailable Qalqon shows the PIN instead — use the Use PIN button.
The PIN is the 4 or 6 digit code you chose. After several wrong attempts Qalqon temporarily blocks further attempts and shows how long to wait.
Qalqon asks for the PIN again
The unlock is per session: after a restart, a logout or when the app is closed by the system, the parent area locks again. This is intended so a child cannot open the parent controls.
Screen time needs a child selected as the screen-time target and the Usage Access permission. If usage cannot be read, Qalqon says so rather than showing zero.
